Purpose of the alpha

Alpha product and methodology test. Run 1 produces a North Macedonia diagnostic (run 1a) and a comparator pilot (run 1b), and tests the end-to-end workflow, source collection and processing, extraction and classification, taxonomy and matching, the human review gates, assessment and judgement, outputs, and the usefulness of the review page. Lessons are recorded in the alpha learning log to inform scaling to further chapters, clusters and countries

Scope Validated

Target country
North Macedonia (MKD)
Thematic scope
(a) All of Chapter 2, Freedom of movement for workers (Cluster 2, Internal market); (b) the technology and AI theme: recommendations materially relating to the areas listed in taxonomy/themes.csv (theme group TECH), wherever they occur in the accession material. Incidental references to technology are out of scope. The full analytical chain is followed for every issue originating from an in-scope Chapter 2 item or technology and AI recommendation. Material outside (a) and (b) is out of scope unless it is needed to follow the chain of an issue already in scope.
Time window
2020-01-01 to the evidence freeze date; earlier material only by logged exception where needed to understand the origin or evolution of an in-scope issue
Language
English primary; Macedonian or Albanian only for core relevant sources with no suitable English version, each recorded in the register; machine translation flagged and capped at Medium confidence
Comparator scope
Run 1b only: two or three reform issues selected at G6, with two or three comparator countries each, approved at G1b

Alpha lessons

Curated lessons from runs/RUN-2026-01/alpha_learning_log.csv. Each is confirmed by the analyst at a gate.

IDAreaLessonScalingStatus
ALN-0001workflowChanging the pilot country from Serbia to North Macedonia before G0 required edits to about thirty files because country, chapter, dates, languages and examples were written into the codebooks, procedures and rules.countries; chaptersValidated implemented
ALN-0002taxonomy matchingA scope combining one chapter with a cross-cutting theme (technology and AI) could not be expressed with chapter and cluster fields alone, so theme tags planned for a later stage had to be brought forward.chapters; clustersValidated accepted
ALN-0003toolingThe helper tools depend on system software (text recognition with Macedonian and Albanian language data, PDF rendering) that was not installed in the working environment and was not recorded anywhere before stage 0.countries; languagesValidated implemented
ALN-0004workflowThe rule that the freeze date falls just after the annual enlargement package did not match the date set at G0: the 2026 package had not appeared by the freeze date, so the newest annual report in the run is from 2025.countries; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0005sourcesA cross-cutting theme makes the whole of each annual report and the screening reports for all clusters relevant, so the EU source base is much larger than for a single chapter.chapters; clusters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0006sourcesMajor publishers (OECD and SIGMA, UNDP, Council of Europe, some Council and national pages) block automated downloads, so several core sources need manual retrieval by the analyst.countries; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0007sourcesAlmost all national government sources in scope are only in Macedonian (some also in Albanian), so most evidence on the country response will rest on machine translation capped at Medium confidence.countries; languagesValidated accepted
ALN-0008toolingAcquisition relied on an unversioned working script; three recording errors were caught and corrected, which shows the step needs a tested tool.countries; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0009workflowSearching for sources with parallel agents, one per group of families, and checking every URL before download found 99 documents in under an hour.countries; chapters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0010extractionIn the sample, the technology theme produced about two and a half times as many items as Chapter 2 (742 against 288), many of them sector IT systems of doubtful relevance, at about 6 to 7 hours of agent time for 11 sources.chapters; clusters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0011toolingThe quote check cannot verify quotes that cross a page break because printed page numbers and running headers sit between the pages, so sound items were shortened or dropped.volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0012extractionParallel extraction agents applied the same rules in different ways where the rules were silent (repeated text, sub-area progress wording, chapter basis), which makes counts and later judgements inconsistent.countries; chapters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0013extractionThe automatic quote check confirms that a quote appears at its location but not that it is cut to the claim; three quotes that began too early passed it unnoticed until an agent re-read them.volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0014extractionApplying analyst decisions R1 to R11 by revising the sample, rather than re-extracting it, took about half an hour per source and cut the sample from 1,054 to 732 items with every quote still verified; it also surfaced the next layer of boundary questions.chapters; countries; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0015review gatesThe manual extraction check was reduced to simplified hand-coding of three passages and a stratified sample of 70 items, focused on missed and misclassified items, instead of reviewing every extracted item.countries; chapters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0016review gatesIndependent agents (a blind coder and reviewers who took no part in extraction) checked all 725 sample items in under 15 minutes elapsed, recorded verdicts before fixing, and gave usable error rates without analyst time.countries; chapters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0017extractionThe main extraction weaknesses are missed neighbouring claims (about 14% of in-scope claims, mostly low or medium importance) and quotes that hold two claims; types and references are almost always right.volume; chaptersValidated accepted
ALN-0018taxonomy matchingThe EU accession material says almost nothing specific about artificial intelligence (two EU requirement items in six years of reports); AI evidence for the country comes mainly from a national audit, so an AI focus cannot rest on EU requirements alone.chapters; countriesValidated accepted
ALN-0019taxonomy matchingDrafting the taxonomy in two parallel parts (Chapter 2 and technology) produced an overlapping issue on electronic exchange of social security data, because each drafter treated the shared items as its own.chapters; clustersValidated accepted
ALN-0020taxonomy matchingA draft theme issue with no supporting recommendation reached the G4 package, although procedure P2 requires one, because no tool tests this rule and the drafter only hinted at it in a note.chapters; clusters; volumeValidated accepted
ALN-0021toolingText conversion left pages with a heading over an image body almost empty, because text recognition only ran on near-empty pages; one regulator's full recommendations were missing until an extraction agent noticed.countries; languages; volumeProposed
ALN-0022extractionThe second pass added 13.6% more items on non-EU sources but only 2.7% on EU sources, so the same check may have been applied unevenly.volume; chaptersProposed
